chapters.fx: What to watch: U Mich sentiment 9am CT (consensus 47.5; the 5–10y inflation expectations, last 3.4%, matter more than the headline) and Collins at 3pm CT. Then the swing event: CPI Wed Oct 14, 7:30am CT — core m/m of 0.2% or below validates disinflation; 0.3%+ revives October (currently ~17–19%).
chapters.meaning: What it means: confirms the prior thesis. The hawkish chorus all spoke Thursday — Waller (more hikes probably needed, flexible on timing), Musalem (rates may need to climb 6–9 more months), Kashkari (one more this year, another in 2027). The Iran de-escalation shaves the war premium, not the rate repricing: the dollar is softer on risk, not on the Fed.
numbers: What changed: the dollar slips off 18-month highs as Trump rules out new Iran strikes before the Nov 3 midterms — DXY ~102.02–102.13 (−0.1%); US 10Y 5.232% (−4.9bp) after a strong $22B 30Y auction (stop 5.618%, highest since 2000); Brent −0.7% to $103.53.

Thread: the hawkish-hold thesis is in its third week — FOMC minutes had 'most' seeing another hike by year-end, Dec is ~83% priced, and claims came in at 197k (fourth straight week near 57-year lows) keeping the labor floor intact.
DXY is down about 0.2 from 102.22–102.30 yesterday; all quotes are indicative, not executable prices.

scenarios.base: Fed holds its hawkish tone into the Oct 27–28 FOMC; USD stays bid while Dec hike odds hold near 80%+.
scenarios.bear: Soft CPI or a dovish FOMC surprise collapses hike odds; crowded USD longs unwind.
scenarios.bull: Oct 14 CPI beats expectations — Dec gets fully priced and DXY extends to fresh highs.

chapters.title: US Dollar

chapters.fx: What to watch: French budget bills hit the National Assembly plenary Oct 13, key votes late Nov–mid Dec, and an Aa3 rating review this month. On the chart, 1.1161 is the line: a break risks 1.1065; a hold plus fading fiscal fear opens a relief bounce toward 1.13.
chapters.meaning: What it means: breaks the relief-bounce hope from yesterday's edition. ECB chief economist Lane added a dovish tint — higher borrowing costs could curb demand and reduce the need for further tightening — against market pricing of ~80% for another ECB hike by year-end. Spain's snap election (PM Sánchez, after housing measures were rejected) adds political noise. The fiscal risk premium is off the wides, but it is not gone.
numbers: What changed: EUR/USD ~1.1211, off Monday's 17-month low of 1.1161; the French selloff stabilizes — French 10Y briefly topped 5% (first time since July 2002) before Le Pen's €25B/yr spending-cut plan pulled yields down ~11bp; OAT–Bund spread ~140–146bp, off the >150bp wides (widest since 2011/12).
Thread: the euro has fallen four straight weeks — French fiscal stress layering a sovereign risk premium onto the ECB-policy drag.
EUR/GBP at 84.74 pence is a 16-month low; EUR/CHF ~0.9324 steady after its biggest weekly fall in 17 months.

scenarios.base: EUR/USD pinned near 1.12; French fiscal headlines keep a risk premium on EUR.
scenarios.bull: 1.1161 holds, budget process calms spreads — relief toward 1.13.

chapters.title: Euro

chapters.fx: What to watch: September CPI (consensus ~3.5% — release date unconfirmed, not stated here); Chancellor Healey's first Budget on Oct 28; S&P's UK rating review today; BoE decision Nov 5.
chapters.meaning: What it means: confirms the hawkish-hold thesis. Inflation is still the story in Britain, and the Bank is leaning against it even as gilt markets wobble on fiscal fears. The pound is the relative winner of Europe's fiscal stress so far — bid vs the euro, riding the dollar's softness.
numbers: What changed: GBP/USD ~1.3228, slightly higher on a softer dollar; sterling at a 16-month high vs the euro (EUR/GBP 84.74p) as French contagion fears push money toward London.
Thread: the BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6–3 vote — three members wanted another hike; UK CPI was 3.1% in August and the BoE sees ~3.75% in Q4, slightly above 4% early 2027.
The BoE also paused gilt sales for six months and halted long-dated sales — a fiscal-stress valve.

scenarios.base: GBP consolidates the 1.32 area; hawkish-hold keeps a floor under it.
scenarios.bear: Dovish BoE or fiscal wobble — GBP gives back the euro-driven gains.
scenarios.bull: Hot UK CPI revives hike bets — GBP/USD pushes higher.

chapters.title: British Pound

chapters.fx: What to watch: BoJ Oct 29–30; any US CPI surprise that moves the US 10Y moves this pair first.
chapters.meaning: What it means: confirms the hiking-cycle thesis — the Oct 29–30 BoJ meeting is live. The tension is pure: the haven bid softens as Iran fears ease (yen-positive forces fading), but the wide yield gap caps any yen rally. Intervention watch stays on if USD/JPY pushes toward 160.
numbers: What changed: USD/JPY 158.05 — steady; the dollar gained ~0.1% vs the yen overnight, the only G10 pair where USD rose. BoJ branch managers (Oct 8) said cost-push price pressure is broadening to consumer businesses; Governor Ueda flagged that underlying inflation could overshoot 2% and signaled continued tightening intent; OIS prices a December hike above 80%.
Thread: the US–Japan rate gap has owned this pair — 24-year-high US 10Y against a BoJ at 1.25%.
Japan's August current account surplus (¥4.062T) beat, and PM Takaichi is pushing food-consumption-tax cuts funded without new bonds.

scenarios.base: Rate gap dominates; USD/JPY consolidates below the 159–160 resistance zone.
scenarios.bear: US yields push higher — USD/JPY tests 160 and intervention talk returns.
scenarios.bull: Risk-off escalation or dovish Fed repricing — JPY rallies, USD/JPY breaks lower.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen

chapters.fx: What to watch: any Iran/Saudi headlines overnight; if Tehran confirms the talks track, expect further haven unwind (CHF softer).
chapters.meaning: What it means: mildly breaks the escalating-haven-bid thesis — the fear trade is leaking out of CHF as the strike headlines fade. With the SNB pinned at 0.00% (next decision Dec 10), the franc remains a pure geopolitical play, not a rates story.
numbers: What changed: USD/CHF ~0.832 — the franc gained ~0.2% overnight on safe-haven demand, but the haven bid is softening as Trump de-escalates; EUR/CHF ~0.9324 steady.
Thread: the franc was the haven of choice this week — Iran/Hormuz escalation plus French bond stress both bid it.

scenarios.base: CHF drifts as the haven bid unwinds gradually; USD/CHF holds the low-0.83s.
scenarios.bear: Confirmed Hormuz reopening — CHF gives back the week's gains.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation — haven flows flood back into CHF.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc

chapters.fx: What to watch: China CPI Wed Oct 14; RBA next meets Nov 2–3 (was the Sep 29 hike one-and-done?); any Iran headlines flip risk sentiment fast.
chapters.meaning: What it means: confirms the de-escalation relief thesis for risk proxies — oil still above $103 keeps the commodity bid, and a softer dollar does the rest. AUD/JPY ~110.6 stays capped by the US–Japan rate gap spilling into yen crosses.
numbers: What changed: AUD/USD ~0.70 (+0.26%) — the best G10 performer as the dollar softened and yields eased; RBA on hold at 4.60% with a hawkish stance; China reopened after Golden Week ended Oct 7.
Thread: the Aussie has been squeezed between a hiking RBA and risk-off flows — the risk proxy with the best policy tailwind in G10.

scenarios.base: AUD firms with risk sentiment; 0.70 holds while de-escalation lasts.
scenarios.bear: Re-escalation or hot US CPI — AUD/NZD give back the relief rally first.
scenarios.bull: Confirmed Hormuz reopening + soft US CPI — risk-on, AUD extends.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar

chapters.fx: What to watch: Canada jobs 7:30am CT today; BoC decision + MPR Oct 28 (13:45 UTC).
chapters.meaning: What it means: confirms the oil-bid thesis — the physical market is still tight even as the fear premium leaks. A soft jobs print would reinforce the BoC's neutral-to-dovish lean; a beat with $103 oil complicates it.
numbers: What changed: USD/CAD ~1.42 (−0.4% vs prior session) — the loonie supported by Brent above $103; Canada's September jobs report lands today at 7:30am CT (consensus +6.1K, unemployment 6.5% vs 6.4%, after −41.7K).
Thread: CAD has been the terms-of-trade winner of the oil spike; the BoC sits neutral at 2.25% with its Oct 28 decision + MPR next.
The supply-shock premium is intact despite de-escalation: Hormuz crude crossings down 27% to 10.1 mbd (2-month low), and Hurricane Isaias shut 62.9% of Gulf of Mexico output (~1.3 mbd).

scenarios.base: CAD stays supported while Brent holds above ~$100; USD/CAD drifts lower on oil.
scenarios.bear: Jobs miss + de-escalation unwinds the oil premium — USD/CAD bounces.
scenarios.bull: Jobs beat + oil firm — CAD extends gains into the BoC.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar

chapters.fx: What to watch: RBNZ decision Oct 28 (01:00 UTC) — pause vs hike is now a genuine two-way bet; dairy prices and oil as the swing factors.
chapters.meaning: What it means: breaks the 'October hike likely' lean — if the RBNZ pauses, the hawkish repricing unwinds and NZD softens. The pause call rests on an uneven recovery, not on inflation being beaten.
numbers: What changed: NZD/USD ~0.5615 (+0.2%) on the softer dollar and easing yields; Westpac now expects the RBNZ to pause on Oct 28 and hike 25bp in December (OCR 2.75%), plus two more in early 2027.
Thread: the RBNZ hiked to 2.75% on Sep 2 as fuel inflation ran hot; the market had ~75% priced for another hike in October.

scenarios.base: NZD drifts with risk sentiment; RBNZ pause priced in gradually.
scenarios.bear: RBNZ pauses and sounds done — NZD underperforms the commodity bloc.
scenarios.bull: RBNZ hikes Oct 28 after all — NZD re-rates higher.

headline: The dollar pauses as Trump takes an Iran strike off the table — the war premium leaks out, but the Fed's hawkish-hold thesis stands.
